record.original_question: Let n be a positive integer. For a finite group K and an automorphism n−1 ϕ of K of order dividing n, let Xn,ϕ (K):= {x ∈ K | xxϕ · · · xϕ = 1}. Let cn be the supremum of the ratios |Xn,ϕ (H)|/|H| over all finite groups H and their automorphisms ϕ ∈ Aut(H) such that ϕn = id and Xn,ϕ (H) ̸= H. (a) Let n > 1 be a positive integer such that cd < 1 for all prime power divisors d of n. Is it true that cn < 1? (b) For a finite group G and a positive integer n, the generalized Hughes–Thompson subgroup is defined as Hn(G) = ⟨x ∈ G | xn ̸= 1⟩. Suppose that n is a positive integer for which there is a positive integer kn depending only on n such that |G: Hn(G)| ⩽ kn for all finite groups G with Hn(G) ̸= 1. Is it true that then cn < 1? This question is open even when n ⩾ 5 is prime.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. For a finite group $K$ and an automorphism $\phi \in \mathrm{Aut}(K)$ whose order divides $n$, define
$$X_{n,\phi}(K) := \{x \in K \mid x \cdot x^\phi \cdot x^{\phi^2} \cdots x^{\phi^{n-1}} = 1\}.$$
Define
$$c_n := \sup \left\{ \frac{|X_{n,\phi}(H)|}{|H|} \;\Big|\; H \text{ a finite group},\ \phi \in \mathrm{Aut}(H),\ \phi^n = \mathrm{id},\ X_{n,\phi}(H) \neq H \right\}.$$

For a finite group $G$ and a positive integer $n$, define the generalized Hughes–Thompson subgroup
$$H_n(G) := \langle x \in G \mid x^n \neq 1 \rangle.$$

Answer the following:

(a) Suppose $n > 1$ is such that $c_d < 1$ for every prime-power divisor $d$ of $n$. Must $c_n < 1$?

(b) Suppose $n$ is such that there exists a positive integer $k_n$ (depending only on $n$) with $|G : H_n(G)| \leq k_n$ for every finite group $G$ with $H_n(G) \neq 1$. Must $c_n < 1$?

In particular, resolve these questions in the case when $n \geq 5$ is a prime.
